- When sentiment is negative (especially strong negative spikes), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to compensate for sentiment-driven downside risk.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices pulling back from highs), model often fails to anticipate — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in next 2–4 periods.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high or adjust downward if sentiment weakens.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 3–7% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.05.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag — delay correction by 1–2 periods and adjust downward gradually.  
- When true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
